newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mostly weaker.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mostly weaker after units again carved out and respected afternoon trading ranges following a busy morning.
Traders linked currencies' moves lower mainly to the inability of most units to follow through on Wednesday's advance.

In particular, they said yen's strong surge yesterday lacked extension and appeared driven by shortcovering. They noted that open interest in lead-month December yen fell 10,094 on Wednesday, a hefty drop considering that total open interest in the contract was 69,701.
"There was a shakeout in the yen," said a currency floor broker of the Japanese unit's rise Wednesday on falling open interest.
"I think it was a lot of shortcovering," said another broker of Wednesday's yen rally. "I think it (Thursday's pullback) was basically a retracement of yesterday."

Others said currencies also drew some sellers on signs of more vigor than expected in the U.S. economy which reminded traders that Federal Reserve policymakers might see a need to hike rates on Tuesday.
August housing starts rose 4.5 percent to a 1.525-million unit annual rate, above forecasts for 1.445 million units.
Both price components of September Philadelphia Federal Reserve business activity index diverged from the drop in the overall index and surged, fanning inflation jitters.
Comments by various U.S. officials scattered throughout the trading session had little effect.
But heading into Tuesday's open market committee meeting, traders had not expected much in the way of economy-related remarks from Fed officials who must observe the so-called "black-out" period.
Technically, December marks approached and respected support at $0.6632, last Friday's low, but stayed well shy of resistance pegged at $0.6690, a tick above Thursday's peak.
Sterling slid on signs of good fund sales early in futures that hit sellstops that carried December futures from 1.5560 to the day's low, brokers said.
Brokers also noted signs of cash sales overseas of pounds for yen and sales of yen for Swiss francs.
December yen filled a chart gap up to Wednesday's settlement at $0.009278 from Thursday's gap-lower open, and then it failed again.
Nearby Canadian dollar recovered after holding trendline support at $0.7313, with a double-bottom penciled in at $0.7314 reinforcing that area.
"It's well, well supported," said a floor broker of the Canadian unit. "I think they're going to rally."
He pegged a first target at $0.7335 and then $0.7345.

Dec yen lost $0.000028 to $0.009250, marks lost $0.0020 to $0.6646, Swiss francs eased $0.0008 to $0.8117, Sterling fell $0.0080 to $1.5520, Canadian dollar firmed $0.0003 to $0.7320, Aussie dollar rose $0.0034 to $0.7889, Mexican peso fell $0.000325 to $0.125875. -Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
